definitions.explanation: A Japanese herb (Cryptotaenia japonica) with three-lobed leaves and a mild, celery-like flavor. Widely used as a garnish and aromatic in Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: ⟦{茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}し→茶碗蒸し：17312_chawanmushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{三|み}つ{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧のせる。
examples.english: To place mitsuba on top of chawanmushi.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{吸|す}い{物|もの}→お吸い物：15773_osuimono⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仕上|しあ}げ→仕上げ：11519_shiage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{三|み}つ{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}えた→添える：13315_soeru⟧。
examples.english: I added mitsuba as a finishing touch to the clear soup.

examples.japanese: {三|み}つ{葉|ば}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{和食|わしょく}→和食：10436_washoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{彩|いろど}り→彩り：12506_irodori⟧や{風味|ふうみ}{付|づ}け⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: Mitsuba has a pleasant aroma, so it is often used to add color and flavor to Japanese dishes.

notes:
WRITING:
The name literally means "three leaves" ({三|み}つ{葉|ば}), referring to its distinctive three-lobed leaf structure.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Mitsuba is a staple herb in Japanese cooking, used similarly to how parsley or cilantro is used in Western cuisine. It is commonly added to ⟦{茶碗蒸|ちゃわんむ}し→茶碗蒸し：17312_chawanmushi⟧ (savory egg custard), ⟦{親子丼|おやこどん}→親子丼：17621_oyakodon⟧ (chicken and egg rice bowl), and clear soups. It wilts quickly when heated, so it is typically added at the very end of cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三|み}つ{葉|ば}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{添|そ}える→添える：13315_soeru⟧: to garnish with mitsuba
- {三|み}つ{葉|ば}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧: the aroma of mitsuba
